name: @argszero/cordis-plugin-permission-restore-guard
description: Makes a session openable again when its recorded permission preset can no longer be restored. `dsh-permission-presets` writes and restores the same identity on two different terms: switching a session to the Auto preset runs `this.autoAdmit?.()` and silently succeeds with no integration registered, while restoring that session throws 'cannot restore preset "auto" without its active integration'. Because the throw happens inside the service's own `session/created` listener, and `dsh-session`'s announce() lets a throwing listener veto publication, the session is disposed, the client is told api-session/removed and the row leaves the sidebar — with its log intact and no way in the product to open it again. This plugin records a restorable identity first, from a listener prepended to `session/created`, so the refusal never fires: one `permission/preset` event naming a configured preset with the same knobs, or the identity the picker itself will report. It writes no knob, so no session's sandbox mode or approval policy changes. A tool reports and repairs sessions already in that state.
